newsitem.title: USA: FCOJ futures close weaker and in range, await data.
newsitem.headline: FCOJ futures close weaker and in range, await data.

text.p: FCOJ futures closed lower as the market awaited next week's U.S. Department of Agriculture crop estimate to gauge its next move, market sources said.

The estimate of Florida's 1996/97 crop, released Wednesday, will account for losses from the January 19 freeze. So far, players have had only anecdotal information and an unofficial estimate by Tropicana on which to gauge losses.
Tropicana last week estimated that up to seven percent of the crop would be lost to the cold weather. The USDA put the crop at record 220 million 90-lb boxes before the freeze.
Support was seen at 84.00 cents and resistance at 90.00 cents basis March.
The spot month settled 1.50 lower at 85.05 cents, having ranged from 86.20 to 84.50 cents. The deferred contracts ended down 1.55 to 3.05.

Cold temperatures that could reach Florida late next week are not expected to fall low enough to harm fruit, forecasters said. They stressed that traders should continue to monitor the airmass, since it is too early to predict temperatures.
